gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-tc: Noto Sans TC lets its curves flare outward rather than curl inward, giving each letter generous room to breathe. Junegull's pinched, closed shapes add retro bounce while the body stays open.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-thai-lo: Junegull draws curves and stems with no swelling or thinning, and every curve pinches shut at its mouth. Noto Sans Thai Looped has spacious curve endings and big-bodied lowercase, so extended reading feels open and unhurried.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-parkinsans: Junegull is retro and friendly, with closed, pinched curves and no stroke contrast. Parkinsans holds one stroke thickness throughout and opens its round letters, so paragraphs of text stay crisp and modern at small sizes.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-pt-sans-caption: Friendly retro charm up top, with Junegull holding every line to one thickness and pinching its curves nearly shut. Below it, PT Sans Caption opens its bowls and loosens the mood.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-questrial: Junegull brings a retro, friendly look with pinched curves and a lowercase as stout as cast iron capitals. And Questrial's flat, stencil-cut strokes keep paragraphs feeling light and open.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-radio-canada: Radio Canada stands full and clear, with no pressure variation in its line. Junegull's closed, pinched curves against Radio Canada's open endings is what defines this pairing: retro and friendly above, crisp and clear below.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-roboto: Retro swagger up top, with sturdy clarity waiting below. Junegull excels at pinched, nib-drawn character and sheer lowercase presence, while Roboto keeps its generous round letters open and legible.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-sarpanch: Junegull draws every line like a drafting pen, steady and friendly, with curves pinched at the mouth. But Sarpanch opens the mouth of its e clearly, and that open-against-closed tension defines the pair.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Junegull draws spaghetti-like strokes of one width, and each curve pinches closed for a retro, friendly feel. Schibsted Grotesk leaves its terminals open and its bowls generous, so paragraphs move along smoothly.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-sen: Junegull is retro and friendly, with no stroke contrast and a lowercase that carries the stature of cast iron capitals. Sen traces each letter in constant weight, ending its curves before they turn inward.
